newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka denies military shot at Indian fishermen.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka denies military shot at Indian fishermen.

text.p: Sri Lanka denied on Monday its navy or air force shot at Indian fishermen earlier this month as reported by New Delhi.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement the Indian High Commissioner in Colombo had brought to its notice two incidents involving Indian fishermen.

In one incident it was alleged that two Sri Lankan naval boats fired at fishermen in the Palk Strait on July 14. In the other, Sri Lankan helicopters were said to have attacked fishermen off the Indian coast on July 17.
It said the Indian High Commissioner had asked Sri Lanka to look into the incidents because they had led to resentment among fishermen in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
But the foreign ministry said it was satisfied that the Indian fishermen were not attacked by its forces.
"The Sri Lankan government categorically refutes the monstrous allegation that Sri Lankan aircraft have deliberately intruded deep into Indian territorial waters and attacked fishermen," it said.

The statement said three Indian fishermen, picked up while swimming in northern Sri Lankan waters, had told police their trawler had been fired upon by the Sri Lankan navy. The fishermen said their boat was sunk with two persons on board.
The Foreign Ministry said the navy had investigated the allegations and confirmed that while two Sri Lankan naval boats were in the area, no firing had taken place.

The statement quoted Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar as telling the Indian envoy that the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) were "constantly looking out for opportunities of disrupting the good relations that exist between Sri Lanka and India".
The LTTE are fighting a 14-year-old war with Sri Lankan forces for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
LTTE boats have operated in the Palk Strait that separates India from Sri Lanka and Indian fishermen said last year the rebels were forcing them to carry refugees to Tamil Nadu.
In India on Monday, more than 1,000 people joined a rally at the Sri Lankan deputy high commissioner's office in Tamil Nadu's capital Madras to protest against the killing of the fishermen.
